I've recently started a playthrough again, the first time in 13 years. What is the difference betweeen MGSO and OpenMW? MGSO seems to look better.

MGSO is a large compilation of mods that work well together to balance the game, update it graphically, and fix bugs. OpenMW is a rewrite of the game engine using purely open source technology and it's cross platforn (Windows, OSX, Linux and I think android). The thing is, OpenMW plays and looks roughly the same as the base game, but with many bugs removed that were a part of Morrowind's Gamebryo engine. So all the changes are technical really. Stick to MGSO as it's an objectively better experience, but if you wanted to experience Morrowind pure, or if you value open source software, I'd suggest checking out OpenMW

But my absolute number one favorite is Fallout 2. Because as far as I'm concerned, I won that game, and I never got anywhere near the ending.

For those unfamiliar, you start out as a tribal savage descended from the original vault dweller in Fallout 1. And you are sent out into the world to find a Garden of Eden Creation Kit to save your village, which is dying out due to the harsh climate. Then your entire village gets rounded up and taken prisoner by the remnants of the federal government, and you are supposed to go save them.

I peaced out on my village. Once I got to New Reno, I fucking took over that town. I obliterated the gangs (and in my mind turn them over). I became a heavyweight boxing champion. I was a porn star. And I was also a gambling LORD. I had more money and power than god, and I even had a tricked out car. And when my car got stolen, I executed every mother fucker I saw between me and it.

After all that, I figured it was in keeping with my character that he no longer give a rats ass about their backwater village. Big city life had corrupted him, and to this day in my head canon he's been living the high life in New Reno.

That was my ending to Fallout 2. And it's the only CRPG which facilitated that degree of actual role playing for me.
